records.title: Expected return with the literal time-like label 0100
records.header_literal: B) CM v CZ (20.45 p.m., November 12th); 20.20; RIZI-62
records.meaning: The sender reports an expected return at the literal label 0100. The closing S is not expanded, and this record does not itself identify the returning person or establish a complete itinerary.
notes: All 62 printed coordinates decode directly, with no source erasures, substitutions or frame changes. The following CM UM is printed transmission control outside the body.
RUECKUNFT is retained with only the one K visible in the decoded stream; the standard spelling Rueckkunft would require an extra plaintext letter and is not silently inserted.
0100 is preserved as four literal labels. Its interpretation as a time is contextual; the body does not specify a time zone or independently identify the date.
The neighboring Seifert service exchange does not establish that the abbreviated S here is a particular person.

records.title: A message about attempting to obtain a vehicle
records.header_literal: B) CM v CZ (10.10 a.m., November 14th); RIZI-70
records.meaning: The message concerns trying to obtain a vehicle or wagon. The terse infinitive form alone does not securely distinguish a request to try from a report of an attempt, and Wagen does not by itself identify a specific car or railway wagon.
notes: All 70 native coordinates are retained and valid. High-resolution inspection reads the last group of the first row as FGXAV, including a clear X; the earlier low-resolution Y-like impression is not retained as a fictitious source erasure.

The ordinary-word proposal costs four observed-coordinate substitutions. The literal 6 in I6GENDE… is changed only through an explicit coordinate repair, not through a global reinterpretation of the numeral label.
The edition does not identify a vehicle, promise that one was obtained, or infer a connection to another service message merely from the word Wagen.

prior_credit: Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier repository OCR and unchanged-key outputs are retained separately. Source review and explicit editorial work: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro. No universal first-decipherment priority is asserted.
limits: All native source slots remain in printed order; no insertion, deletion or reordering.
Unknown square cells remain globally coupled and injective. Roundtrip completion witnesses are explicitly nonhistorical.
Observed-coordinate substitutions and source-mask fills are priced separately. A source-compatible word proposal is not proof of unique historical wording.
